verses.english: Linked Discourses 1.39
4. The Host of a Hundred Felicities
With Pajjunna’s Daughter (1st)
So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

verses.pali: Atha kho kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ mahāvanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
verses.english: Then, late at night, the glorious Kokanadā, Pajjunna’s daughter, lighting up the entire Great Wood, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
verses.english: and recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:
“Staying in the woods of Vesālī
is the Buddha, best of creation.
Kokanadā am I who worships him,
Kokanadā, Pajjuna’s daughter.
Previously I had only heard
the teaching realized by the Clear-eyed One.
But now I know it as a witness
while the sage, the Holy One teaches.
There are simpletons who go about
denouncing the teaching of the noble ones.
They fall into the terrible Hell of Screams
where they suffer long.
There are those who have found  <j>acceptance and peace
in the teaching of the noble ones.
After giving up this human body,
they swell the hosts of gods.”
